Study_Title: Semantic Quorum Assurance: Collective Certification for Non-Deterministic AI Infrastructure
Threat_Attacker_Model: Semantically unsafe infrastructure mutations (e.g., destructive cloud/Kubernetes state changes) that pass syntactic IAM, RBAC, and admission webhook checks under single-agent hallucination or prompt injection.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Semantic Quorum Assurance (`SQA`) multi-agent certification quorum coupled with a sovereign execution gate (`Phi_gate`, optionally TEE/hypervisor-isolated) and SHA-256 contract digest binding.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Sovereign Execution Gate (`Phi_gate`) & Multi-Agent Semantic Quorum Verifier.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Collective semantic safety certification before mutative infrastructure execution; SHA-256 integrity binding between certified contract and executed state transition.
Trust_Assumptions: Sovereign execution gate (`Phi_gate`) host/TEE is isolated from proposing agents; independent quorum evaluators do not suffer correlated failures.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 500 infrastructure-inspired mutation scenarios, SQA reduces unsafe approval rate from 18.5% (single-agent validation) to 0.3% (a 61.7x reduction) while adding median validation latency of 1.45–4.12 s across risk tiers (pp. 1–2, 5, 11–14).
Exposed_Security_Function: Risk-tiered multi-agent semantic quorum certification and SHA-256 contract-bound execution gating (`Phi_gate`).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical SHA-256 digests (`STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY`), adds 1.45–4.12 s median quorum latency, and excludes ambiguous edge-case scenarios from the held-out 0.3% unsafe-approval headline metric (p. 1).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 5–10 (pp. 1–2, 5, 11–14): 'On 500 infrastructure-inspired mutation scenarios, with safety results reported on held-out safe/unsafe trials excluding ambiguous scenarios, SQA reduces unsafe approval from 18.5% for single-agent validation to 0.3% while adding median validation latency of 1.45–4.12 seconds across the studied risk buckets... It is bound to the contract via a SHA-256 hash digest.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Semantic Quorum Assurance (SQA) gates mutative AI infrastructure actions behind a risk-tiered multi-agent certification quorum bound via SHA-256 digests to an isolated execution gate (`Phi_gate`), reducing unsafe approvals from 18.5% to 0.3% across 500 scenarios at 1.45–4.12 s median latency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 21-page formal and empirical infrastructure-safety study evaluated across 500 cloud/infrastructure mutation scenarios.
Protected_Object: Cloud/infrastructure state-mutation proposals, SHA-256 certified contracts, and sovereign execution gate (`Phi_gate`) transitions.
Composition_Evidence: Validates intent-to-action semantic safety (B1/B2), enforces SHA-256 contract-bound execution at `Phi_gate` (B3), and logs quorum certificates (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-387 / ARXIV-S-0357) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3;B4); Bukti=FORMAL_MODEL; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (DG;AD).

Enforcement_Point_Location: Remote MCP PaaS Ingress Gateway (`*.run.tools`) & Proposed Schema Transparency Log.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Characterizes ecosystem-wide AS/CDN concentration, OAuth 2.1 PKCE enforcement disparity, and lack of cryptographic tool-schema signing.
Trust_Assumptions: Active TCP/HTTP/OAuth probing across public registries reflects live remote MCP server deployments.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Probes 179 remote MCP endpoints across Smithery and Official registries: 76 (42.5%) accept TCP connections within a 5,000 ms timeout; 95% of commercial PaaS-hosted servers (`*.run.tools`) enforce gateway-level OAuth 2.1 with PKCE S256, whereas self-hosted endpoints largely omit authentication, and 0% cryptographically sign tool schemas (pp. 1–6).
Exposed_Security_Function: Network/TLS/OAuth observability probing (`O0–O2`) and proposed signed Merkle schema transparency logging.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Pilot row CLM-0013 update: upgraded Target_Boundary from B3 to MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3;B4), updated Formal_Evidence_Type from NONE to INFORMAL_ARGUMENT, and PQC_Migration_Stage to STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY (OAuth 2.1 PKCE S256 + X.509 TLS + proposed Merkle tree heads). Sample limited to 76 live endpoints out of 179 registered URLs.

Study_Title: MCP-SandboxScan: WASM-based Secure Execution and Runtime Analysis for MCP Tools
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious or vulnerable third-party MCP tools executing unauthorized filesystem, environment, or network operations or returning poisoned outputs across direct WASM, WASM-shim, and native stdio execution paths.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: WebAssembly (`WASM` / `WASI`) capability-based sandbox isolation paired with `SandScope` behavioral witness detection and OS-level `Docker`/`Bubblewrap` containment.
Enforcement_Point_Location: `MCP-SandboxScan` (`SandScope`) WASM/WASI & Native Stdio Behavioral Audit Layer.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Deterministic capability-scoped WASM/WASI sandboxing and high-precision runtime behavioral witness detection under low-effort evasion transforms.
Trust_Assumptions: WASM/WASI runtime and OS container boundary (`Docker`/`Bubblewrap`) enforce declared capability descriptors.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: On the controlled multi-ecosystem runtime benchmark across Direct-WASM, WASM-Shim, and Native stdio MCP paths (`Table 1`, pp. 7–8), `MCP-SandboxScan` achieves `1.000` precision (`0` false positives), `0.889` recall, and `0.941` F1, with enhanced witness detection outperforming raw substring matching under evasion transforms (`Tables 2–3`, p. 8).
Exposed_Security_Function: WASM/WASI capability sandboxing, native-stdio protocol shimming, and runtime witness behavioral auditing.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Many real-world MCP servers rely on native OS bindings or dynamic runtimes that cannot compile directly to standalone WASM without a native stdio shim (`Table 3`, p. 8), and recall is 0.889 (11.1% false negatives).

Table 1 summarizes the controlled runtime evaluation... achieving precision of 1.000, recall of 0.889, and F1 of 0.941.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: MCP-SandboxScan (`SandScope`) combines WASI/WASM capability sandboxing and native-stdio behavioral auditing with an enhanced witness detector, achieving 1.000 precision, 0.889 recall, and 0.941 F1 across Direct-WASM, WASM-Shim, and Native MCP execution paths.

Protected_Object: MCP tool packages (WASM modules and native stdio servers), WASI capability descriptors, and runtime witness traces.
Composition_Evidence: Audits MCP tool artifacts from installation/discovery (B1/B2) through WASI-sandboxed execution (B3) to behavioral witness logging (B4).

Study_Title: Agent-Fence: Mapping Security Vulnerabilities Across Deep Research Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: 14 attack classes across Deep Research Agents (`Agent-Fence`): boundary violations (`SIV` 31%, `WPA` 27%, `UTI+UTA` 24%, `ATD` 18%), authorization confusion, retrieval/memory poisoning, planning manipulation, and Denial-of-Wallet retry loops.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: None (auditable exposure-labeling protocol across deep-agent archetypes and configuration hardening via tool-scope narrowing and retry-budget capping).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Deep Research Agent Orchestration Boundary, Tool Scope Gate, and Retry Budget Controller.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Quantifies Mean Security Break Rate (`MSBR`) across deep-research agent archetypes and demonstrates up to 35% break reduction via architectural scoping.
Trust_Assumptions: Dual-reviewer adjudicated exposure annotations (20% stratified audit) and benchmark scenario instantiations accurately reflect production deep-research workflows.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Decomposes deep-research failures into boundary violations (`SIV` 31%, `WPA` 27%, `UTI+UTA` 24%, `ATD` 18%, p. 1) and evaluates Mean Security Break Rate (`MSBR`, `Table 5`, p. 7) across agent archetypes (`Tables 1–4`, pp. 4–7), showing that narrowing tool scopes and isolating memory/planning reduces Poisoning and Planning Manipulation breaks by up to 35% while capping retry budgets mitigates Denial-of-Wallet.
Exposed_Security_Function: Archetype-to-attack exposure mapping (`Agent-Fence`) and configuration-hardening ablation across deep-research agents.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Even after scope narrowing and retry capping (reducing breaks by up to 35%), deep-research agents retain substantial residual vulnerability to indirect web-page injection (`WPA`) and cross-step planning manipulation.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 3–5 (pp. 1, 4–7, Tables 1–5): 'dominated by boundary violations (SIV 31%, WPA 27%, UTI+UTA 24%, ATD 18%), and authorization confusion... Table 5: Mean Security Break Rate (MSBR)... reducing Poisoning and Planning Manipulation breaks by up to 35%, while retry removal significantly lowers Denial-of-Wallet.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Agent-Fence maps security vulnerabilities across Deep Research Agent archetypes, showing that boundary violations (`SIV` 31%, `WPA` 27%, `UTI+UTA` 24%, `ATD` 18%) dominate failures and that narrowing tool scopes and retry budgets reduces Mean Security Break Rate by up to 35%.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 11-page taxonomy and empirical benchmark evaluating Deep Research Agent archetypes across 14 attack classes and multiple configuration policies.
Protected_Object: Web research retrieval streams, multi-step planning states, sub-agent tool scopes, and retry budgets.
Composition_Evidence: Maps how untrusted web retrieval (B1) corrupts planning/delegation (B2), triggers unauthorized tool calls (B3), and evades trace auditing (B4).

Study_Title: Beyond Single-Agent Alignment: Preventing Context-Fragmented Violations in Multi-Agent Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Context-Fragmented Violations (`CFVs`) in enterprise multi-agent systems where individual sub-agent actions appear locally benign in isolation but compose across departmental agents into a global policy breach.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Cryptographically signed Security Taint Tokens (`STTs`) using `Ed25519` digital signatures and `HMAC-SHA256` message authentication codes (optionally anchored in hardware `SGX`/`TEE` enclaves) propagating monotonic constraint lattices across inter-agent handoffs.
Enforcement_Point_Location: `Distributed Sentinel` Cross-Agent Reference Monitor & `STT` Constraint Propagation Layer.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves Fundamental Limitation of Local Enforcement (Theorem 2.6: no local monitor `E_i` can detect CFVs), Monotonicity of Constraint Propagation (Theorem 2.10), and Completeness of Distributed Enforcement (Corollary 2.11).
Trust_Assumptions: Inter-agent communication bus enforces `Ed25519`/`HMAC-SHA256` STT verification and prevents unmediated side-channel communication.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: On the `PhantomEcosystem` multi-agent benchmark, `Distributed Sentinel` achieves `F1 = 0.95` with `106 ms` end-to-end latency (`16 ms` cryptographic/policy verification + `90 ms` entity extraction on A100), outperforming prompt-based filtering (`F1 = 0.85`) and rule-based DLP (`F1 = 0.65`); ablating STT propagation collapses F1 to `0.53` (pp. 1, 3–6, Theorems 2.6 & 2.10, Corollary 2.11).
Exposed_Security_Function: Ed25519/HMAC-SHA256 Security Taint Token (`STT`) propagation and monotonic distributed constraint verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Resolved UNMAPPED in DAFTAR_442 to MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3;B4). Relies on classical Ed25519 and HMAC-SHA256 primitives (`STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY`), and entity extraction contributes 90 ms of the 106 ms per-hop latency on an A100 GPU.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 2–5 (pp. 1, 3–6, Theorems 2.6 & 2.10, Corollary 2.11): 'Theorem 2.6 (Fundamental Limitation of Local Enforcement): For any CFV S, there exists no local enforcement mechanism Ei... Theorem 2.10 (Monotonicity of Constraint Propagation)... Corollary 2.11 (Completeness of Distributed Enforcement)... Distributed Sentinel achieves F1 = 0.95 with 106ms end-to-end latency (16ms verification + 90ms entity extraction on A100), compared to 0.85 F1 for prompt-based filtering and 0.65 for rule-based DLP.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Formalizes Context-Fragmented Violations (CFVs), proving that local per-agent monitors cannot detect them (Theorem 2.6) while monotonic Ed25519/HMAC-SHA256 Security Taint Token (STT) propagation is sound and complete (Theorem 2.10, Corollary 2.11), achieving 0.95 F1 at 106 ms latency (16 ms verification) on PhantomEcosystem.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 34-page formal and empirical multi-agent security paper (Atlassian) proving Theorems 2.6 & 2.10 and Corollary 2.11 and evaluating Distributed Sentinel on PhantomEcosystem.
Protected_Object: Cross-departmental multi-agent messages, Ed25519/HMAC-SHA256 Security Taint Tokens (STTs), and enterprise DLP invariants.
Composition_Evidence: Propagates signed STT constraints from initial user intent (B1) across multi-agent delegation hops (B2) to tool execution gates (B3) and global audit logs (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-392 / ARXIV-S-0375) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3;B4); Bukti=THEORETIC_PROOF; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (DG;AD).

Study_Title: Beyond Single-Agent Alignment: Preventing Context-Fragmented Violations in Multi-Agent Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Fundamental inability of single-agent alignment and local per-agent guardrails (`E_i`) to detect Context-Fragmented Violations (`CFVs`) across multi-agent enterprise workflows (`PhantomEcosystem`).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Formal impossibility proof (`Theorem 2.6`: Fundamental Limitation of Local Enforcement) and ablation removing `STT` cryptographic taint propagation.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Isolated Per-Agent Local Guardrail (`E_i`) without Cross-Agent State Propagation.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves mathematically (`Theorem 2.6`) that for any CFV `S`, no local enforcement mechanism `E_i` inspecting only agent `A_i`'s local context can distinguish safe from violating global executions.
Trust_Assumptions: Individual sub-agents only observe their local task fragment.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Proves `Theorem 2.6` (p. 4) and confirms empirically on `PhantomEcosystem` that local prompt-based filtering reaches only `0.85` F1, rule-based DLP reaches `0.65` F1, and ablating cross-agent `STT` propagation collapses `Distributed Sentinel` from `0.95` F1 down to `0.53` F1 (pp. 1, 3–5).
Exposed_Security_Function: Impossibility proof of local-only multi-agent enforcement (Theorem 2.6) and STT-ablation benchmark.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Establishes the theoretical lower bound motivating cross-agent cryptographic taint tokens (`STTs`).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 2 & Sec. 5 (pp. 3–4): 'Theorem 2.6 (Fundamental Limitation of Local Enforcement). For any CFV S, there exists no local enforcement mechanism Ei... Ablation studies confirm that each component contributes meaningfully, with the system degrading to 0.53 F1 without STT propagation (§5).'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Theorem 2.6 proves that no local per-agent guardrail (`E_i`) can detect Context-Fragmented Violations (CFVs) in multi-agent systems, corroborated by an empirical F1 collapse from 0.95 to 0.53 when cross-agent STT propagation is removed.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Theoretical impossibility theorem (Theorem 2.6) and STT ablation experiment in ARXIV-S-0375.
Protected_Object: Fragmented multi-agent sub-task contexts and local per-agent DLP/prompt filters.
Composition_Evidence: Proves why isolated per-agent checks at B1/B3 fail without cross-agent delegation state propagation at B2.
Coding_Rationale: Klaim sekunder komplementer (CLM-E09-006B untuk S3-392 / ARXIV-S-0375) hasil ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF oleh REVIEWER_2. Kategori=VULNERABILITY_ATTACK_SURFACE, Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE.

Study_Title: PrivacyPeek: Auditing What LLM-Based Agents Acquire, Not Just What They Say
Threat_Attacker_Model: Over-acquisition of sensitive user data ('Acquisition Leak') where LLM agents invoke read/search tools on confidential files or PII unnecessary for the task, even when their final user-facing output omits the secret.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: None (`PrivacyPeek` execution-trace acquisition auditor measuring Conditional Exposure Rate `CER` and Privacy Leakage Rate `PLR` across 7 acquisition behaviors).
Enforcement_Point_Location: PrivacyPeek Acquisition Inspection & Category-Aware System-Prompt Guardrail.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Distinguishes intermediate tool-acquisition privacy breaches (`PLR` / `CER`) from output-only leakage across multi-step agent trajectories.
Trust_Assumptions: Tool-invocation audit logs record all file/database/API read parameters during task execution.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 1,182 test cases and 10 LLM-based agents spanning 7 acquisition behaviors (`Tables 1–2`, pp. 4–5), intermediate Privacy Leakage Rate (`PLR`) ranges from `16.67%` to `57.53%` and Conditional Exposure Rate (`CER`) from `6.77%` (Llama-3.2-3B) to `51.95%` (Claude-Sonnet-4, which also has the highest Task Completion Rate `86.46%`), proving that more capable agents aggressively over-acquire confidential files unless constrained (`Tables 2–5`, pp. 5–10).
Exposed_Security_Function: Trajectory-level acquisition auditing (`CER`, `PLR`, `TCR`) across 1,182 cases and category-aware prompt mitigation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Category-aware system-prompt directives reduce but do not eliminate unnecessary confidential file reads, showing that hard B3 access-control gates are needed alongside trace auditing.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 3–4 (pp. 1, 4–5, Tables 1–2): 'Table 2: Main results on the 1,182 PrivacyPeek cases for the ten LLM-based agents... CER ranges from 6.77% on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct to 51.95% on Claude-Sonnet-4... PLR ranges from 16.67% to 57.53% and exceeds CER for every agent.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: PrivacyPeek audits what LLM agents acquire during tool execution rather than only what they output across 1,182 cases and 10 agents, revealing 16.67%–57.53% Privacy Leakage Rates (peaking at 51.95% CER on high-capability Claude-Sonnet-4) invisible to output-only privacy benchmarks.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 21-page benchmark and empirical study evaluating 10 LLM agents across 1,182 cases and 7 sensitive data-acquisition behaviors.
Protected_Object: Confidential local files, emails, database records, tool-read arguments, and agent execution traces.
Composition_Evidence: Audits how delegated planning (B2) triggers over-privileged read tool invocations (B3) captured by acquisition trace inspection (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-393 / ARXIV-S-0376) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B2;B3;B4); Bukti=INFORMAL_ARGUMENT; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=NOT_DISCUSSED; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (AD;UG).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi adjudikasi lintas-reviewer Stage 3.

Study_Title: TraceAegis: Securing LLM-Based Agents via Hierarchical and Behavioral Anomaly Detection
Threat_Attacker_Model: Tool poisoning, indirect prompt injection, and sequence-based execution-flow hijacking (`AT-C1` content/parameter anomalies and `AT-C2` control-flow/path anomalies) in LLM-based agents.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Hierarchical and behavioral execution-trace anomaly detector (`TraceAegis`) combining legitimate workflow automaton induction with semantic content/argument verification and system-level telemetry.
Enforcement_Point_Location: TraceAegis Hierarchical Runtime & Post-Execution Trace Monitor.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: High-accuracy detection of both semantic argument tampering (`AT-C1`) and valid-tool sequence deviations (`AT-C2`) across flexible multi-path workflows.
Trust_Assumptions: Historical benign execution traces cover valid task workflow permutations; trace collector is intact.

Study_Title: Signing the Transaction but Not the Decision: Whisper Attacks and a Binding Defense for AP2
Threat_Attacker_Model: `Whisper Attacks` on Google's Agent Payments Protocol (`AP2`) — three attack families (Cart Whisper, Merchant Whisper, and Vault Whisper) where indirect prompt injection in product descriptions steers a shopping agent into signing a valid `ECDSA P-256` W3C Verifiable Credential mandate for an attacker-chosen cart, merchant, or payment alias.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: `A-VIP` (Agent-Verified Intent & Payment binding) protocol extension using `ECDSA P-256` W3C Verifiable Credentials, `SHA-256` cart/merchant hash binding, opaque vault capabilities, single-use nonces, and formal verification in the `TLC` (`TLA+`) model checker (`Theorem 1`, Appendix D, p. 6).
Enforcement_Point_Location: `A-VIP` Pre-Signing Intent-to-Cart Binding Gate & Vault Capability Enforcer.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves via `Theorem 1` and `TLC` model checking that under invariants `I1–I4` (`Safety = I1 & I2 & I3 & I4 & VaultWhisperResistance`), no Whisper attack on the LLM context can leak a payment alias, redirect redemption to an unauthorized merchant, or alter the bound cart hash.
Trust_Assumptions: User confirmation UI and credential vault are isolated from the shopping agent's untrusted browsing context; ECDSA P-256 and SHA-256 hold.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: On baseline `AP2`, the three Whisper attack families succeed at `90%`, `56%`, and `73.3%` ASR across evaluated models (with even the most resistant model at `1.2%` ASR, p. 1); `A-VIP` verified by the `TLC` model checker (`Theorem 1`, p. 6) blocks `100%` (`0%` ASR) of Cart, Merchant, and Vault Whisper attacks with negligible cryptographic binding overhead (~3.8 ms range, pp. 1, 3–8, Tables 1–2).
Exposed_Security_Function: Formal `TLA+/TLC` model checking (`I1–I4`, Theorem 1) + cryptographic intent-to-cart/merchant/vault binding (`A-VIP`) evaluated on AgentDojo-style shopping benchmarks.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical `ECDSA P-256` W3C Verifiable Credentials and `SHA-256` digests (`STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY`), and requires user confirmation of the high-level merchant/budget anchor prior to browsing.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 3–6 (pp. 1–2, 6–8, Theorem 1, Tables 1–2): 'By default, the three attacks succeeded at rates of 90%, 56%, and 73.3%, respectively... Appendix D formalizes these invariants and checks them with the TLC model checker... Theorem 1. Under I1-I4, no Vault Whisper landing on A's LLM context can cause a third-party payment_method_alias to leave the vault...'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Demonstrates that Whisper Attacks hijack baseline AP2 shopping agents at 90%, 56%, and 73.3% ASR despite valid ECDSA P-256 signatures, and proposes `A-VIP`—formally verified in the TLC model checker (Theorem 1, invariants I1–I4)—to bind user intent to merchant, cart hash, and opaque vault tokens.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 22-page attack, defense, and TLA+/TLC formal verification paper auditing Google's AP2 protocol across three Whisper attack families.

Study_Title: Can LLM Infer Risk Information From MCP Server System Logs?

Table 1: Mapping of CE-MCP threats to MAESTRO layers... evaluated across 10 MCP servers (Table 3).'

Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) vulnerabilities in closed-source or credential-gated third-party MCP servers where source code, binaries, and live OAuth tokens (e.g., paid Slack `usergroups:write` tokens) are unavailable to security auditors.

Study_Title: Device Context Protocol: A Compact, Safety-First Architecture for LLM-Driven Control of Constrained Devices
Threat_Attacker_Model: Hallucinated or prompt-injected LLM tool calls issuing out-of-range, unsafe, or unauthorized actuator commands to resource-constrained physical microcontrollers (MCUs) that cannot run heavyweight JSON/HTTP MCP stacks (74 KB RAM in IoT-MCP).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Device Context Protocol (`DCP`): compact binary `CBOR`/`COBS`/`CRC` wire framing paired with scoped, time-limited `HMAC-SHA256` capability tokens (`SHA-256` digests) and deterministic on-MCU range, type, and dry-run safety checks.
Enforcement_Point_Location: `DCP` Python Bridge & On-MCU (`ESP32`/`ESP32-S3`) Deterministic Capability + Range + Dry-Run Verifier.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographically scoped (`HMAC-SHA256`) and physically bounded (range/type/dry-run) command execution on sub-kilobyte RAM microcontrollers.
Trust_Assumptions: Shared `HMAC-SHA256` key provisioned on the MCU and physical safety bounds in firmware are intact.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Reference `ESP32` firmware requires only `27.6 KB` flash and `0.6 KB` RAM (`123x` smaller RAM footprint than `IoT-MCP`'s `74 KB`); on identical `ESP32-S3` hardware, full `DCP` validation (`HMAC-SHA256` capability + range + dry-run + `CBOR`/`COBS`/`CRC`) completes a round-trip in `~15.6 ms` median (within `5 µs` of unvalidated newline-JSON and `13x` faster than IoT-MCP's `~205 ms`, pp. 1–2).
Exposed_Security_Function: HMAC-SHA256 capability tokens, CBOR/COBS/CRC binary framing, and on-MCU range/type/dry-run pre-execution gating.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on symmetric `HMAC-SHA256` tokens (`STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY`; symmetric HMAC is Grover-resilient at 256-bit key lengths but lacks asymmetric non-repudiation).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 1–4 (pp. 1–2): 'Reference firmware measures 27.6 KB flash / 0.6 KB RAM on ESP32... DCP's full schema validation (capability + range + dry-run + CBOR/COBS/CRC) and an IoT-MCP-style newline-JSON wire both complete a round-trip in ~15.6 ms median, within 5 µs of each other... Capability tokens (HMAC-SHA256, scoped, time-limited) bound the LLM's reach; range, type, and dry-run checks reject hallucinated calls before they traverse the wire.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Device Context Protocol (DCP) secures LLM control of constrained microcontrollers using HMAC-SHA256 capability tokens, CBOR/COBS/CRC framing, and dry-run range checks in 27.6 KB flash / 0.6 KB RAM on ESP32 (vs. 74 KB for IoT-MCP) with ~15.6 ms median round-trip latency.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 15-page embedded systems and security paper with open-source ESP32/ESP32-S3 firmware, Python bridge, and conformance benchmark.
Protected_Object: MCU actuator commands, HMAC-SHA256 capability tokens, and CBOR/COBS/CRC wire frames.
Composition_Evidence: Enforces HMAC-SHA256 capability scoping at delegation (B2) and deterministic range/dry-run checks before physical MCU actuation (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-424 / ARXIV-S-0457) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B2;B3); Bukti=INFORMAL_ARGUMENT; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (DG;AD).

Study_Title: From Prompt Injection to Web Exploitation: Revisiting Classic Vulnerabilities in LLM-Integrated Applications

Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that LLM safety guardrails fail to block SSRF payloads when framed as legitimate summarization/translation/webhook tool tasks unless network-layer egress filtering is enforced.

Assessed_Claim_Scope: 28-page vulnerability study bridging prompt injection to backend web exploitation (`LLM2SSRF`) across multiple LLM models.

Study_Title: The Proxy Knows Too Much: Sealing LLM API Routers with Attested TEEs
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious LLM API routers (application-layer MITM proxies that terminate client TLS and hold plaintext prompts, tool calls, and API keys) performing prompt/credential snooping, tool-argument tampering, model downgrade, and audit evasion.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Hardware Trusted Execution Environment (`TEE` / Intel `SGX` enclave) sealing the API router with reproducible build measurement anchoring (`Lemma 1`), client-to-enclave and enclave-to-provider attested TLS channels, and formal protocol verification in `ProVerif` (`Theorem 1` Confidentiality, `Theorem 2` Faithful Relay & Integrity, `Lemma 2` Accountability).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Attested TEE-Sealed LLM API Router Enclave & `ProVerif`-Verified Relay Protocol.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves equal-leakage confidentiality (`Theorem 1`), faithful relay and integrity (`Theorem 2`), and measurement-anchored accountability (`Lemmas 1–2`) against a privileged malicious router host, bounded by a mechanized `ProVerif` model.
Trust_Assumptions: Hardware TEE (`SGX`) guarantees enclave execution integrity and remote attestation authenticity; reproducibility build recipe is publicly auditable.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Blocks `100%` (`4 / 4`) of malicious API router attack classes that succeed on plaintext routers, with formal `ProVerif` verification bounding residual host influence and adding only `5.7 ms` median (`6.3 ms` p95) per-request latency overhead on small request bodies across 3 provider-native workloads and seeded coding-agent audits (pp. 2, 7–9, Theorems 1–2, Lemmas 1–2, Figure 4a).
Exposed_Security_Function: SGX enclave router sealing, reproducible measurement anchoring, and mechanized `ProVerif` protocol verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Relies on classical TEE remote attestation and TLS cryptographic primitives (`STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY`), and does not hide packet-size or timing metadata (`equal-leakage` confidentiality in Theorem 1).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. IV–VI (pp. 1–2, 7–9, Theorems 1–2, Lemmas 1–2, Fig. 4a): 'All four attack classes succeed on a plaintext-access baseline and are blocked by our design; adaptive malicious-router tests and a scoped model in the ProVerif protocol verifier [5] bound the host's remaining influence... Theorem 1 (Confidentiality)... Theorem 2 (Faithful relay and integrity)... For a small request body the added latency has a median of 5.7 ms and a 95th percentile of 6.3 ms (Figure 4a).'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Seals third-party LLM API routers inside attested TEE enclaves with reproducible measurement anchoring, proving confidentiality and faithful relay via security reductions (Theorems 1–2, Lemmas 1–2) and `ProVerif` verification while blocking all 4 router MITM attack classes at 5.7 ms median (6.3 ms p95) latency overhead.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 16-page cryptographic systems and formal verification paper combining game-based proofs (Theorems 1–2), `ProVerif` mechanization, and TEE router benchmarks.
Protected_Object: In-flight client-to-router-to-provider LLM prompts, tool calls, API credentials, and TEE attestation quotes.
Composition_Evidence: Protects delegated model/tool requests in transit (B2/B3) and anchors router code measurements for verifiable auditing (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-427 / ARXIV-S-0464) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B2;B3;B4); Bukti=TOOL_SUPPORTED_VERIFICATION; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (DG;AD).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi adjudikasi lintas-reviewer Stage 3.

Study_Title: The Proxy Knows Too Much: Sealing LLM API Routers with Attested TEEs
Threat_Attacker_Model: Four application-layer MITM attack classes executed by untrusted plaintext LLM API routers (prompt/credential snooping, tool-call argument tampering, silent model downgrade, and log/billing falsification).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Empirical attack reproduction against unsealed plaintext API routers vs. attested SGX enclave routers.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Third-Party LLM API Router TLS Termination Boundary.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates 100% exploitability of all 4 attack classes on standard plaintext API routers due to TLS termination.
Trust_Assumptions: Standard API router terminates client TLS and holds raw bearer keys and JSON payloads in host memory.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: `4 / 4` (`100%`) of evaluated router attack classes succeed silently on the plaintext-access router baseline without client detection, whereas all 4 are blocked by the attested TEE router design at `5.7 ms` median (`6.3 ms` p95) latency cost (pp. 1–2, 7–9).
Exposed_Security_Function: Adversarial router MITM testing across 4 attack classes and 3 provider-native agent workloads.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Plaintext routers cannot be secured by transport-layer HTTPS alone because the router itself is the TLS endpoint.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. I–VI (pp. 1–2, 8–9): 'A router terminates the client's transport-layer security session and opens a separate upstream session, so it holds the full interaction in plaintext. This makes the router an application-layer man-in-the-middle... All four attack classes succeed on a plaintext-access baseline and are blocked by our design.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Demonstrates that standard LLM API routers act as application-layer MITMs due to TLS termination, allowing all 4 evaluated attack classes (snooping, tool tampering, model downgrade, billing/log forgery) to succeed at 100% on plaintext routers.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Baseline plaintext-router vulnerability evaluation across 4 attack classes in ARXIV-S-0464.
Protected_Object: Terminated TLS sessions, plaintext JSON prompts/tool calls, and upstream API keys.
Composition_Evidence: Exposes the MITM trust gap when agents delegate model and tool calls through third-party API routers (B2/B3).
Coding_Rationale: Klaim sekunder komplementer (CLM-E09-041B untuk S3-427 / ARXIV-S-0464) hasil ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF oleh REVIEWER_2. Kategori=VULNERABILITY_ATTACK_SURFACE, Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE.

Study_Title: ACE: A Security Architecture for LLM-Integrated App Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect prompt injection and cross-app control-flow/data-flow hijacking in interleaved plan-execute LLM-integrated app systems.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Abstract-Concrete-Execute (`ACE`) decouples planning from untrusted execution outputs by generating a complete restricted Python abstract execution plan upfront from the trusted user query, validated by static Information-Flow Control (`IFC`) analysis and executed inside isolated worker containers.
Enforcement_Point_Location: `ACE` Trusted Orchestrator, Static Information-Flow Analyzer, and Isolated App Execution Workers.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Guarantees that untrusted third-party app outputs cannot alter the control-flow graph of the pre-committed abstract execution plan or violate static information-flow policies.
Trust_Assumptions: Initial user prompt, ACE orchestrator, and OS container isolation boundary are trusted.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Achieves `0%` indirect prompt injection ASR across control-flow and data-flow benchmarks where interleaved baselines fail, with end-to-end query completion times on `GPT-4.1` of `11.73 s` (Single Tool) and `20.95 s` (Multiple Tool) (`Tables III–IV`, pp. 12–13).
Exposed_Security_Function: Upfront abstract Python plan generation from trusted user intent + static information-flow analysis + isolated concrete execution (`ACE`).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Pilot row CLM-0008 update: updated Boundary_Codes to B1;B2;B3 and replaced the 'PARAFRASA, bukan kutipan verbatim' placeholder with a direct verbatim quote from Section I & IV (pp. 2, 7–13). I & IV–V (pp. 2, 7–13, Tables III–IV): 'Our abstract planning mechanism stands in stark contrast to the majority of existing LLM-based systems, which follow an interleaved plan-execute procedure to determine execution traces and produce a response... Table IV: GPT-4.1 Single Tool total 11.73 s; Multiple Tool 20.95 s.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: ACE (Abstract-Concrete-Execute) prevents indirect prompt injection by compiling trusted user queries into upfront restricted Python abstract plans verified via static information-flow analysis before isolated worker execution, achieving 11.73 s single-tool and 20.95 s multi-tool total runtime on GPT-4.1.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 24-page security architecture paper (Northeastern University) evaluating ACE across single-tool and multi-tool prompt-injection benchmarks.
Protected_Object: Trusted user queries, restricted Python abstract plans, static IFC labels, and isolated third-party app outputs.

Enforcement_Point_Location: Inference-Time Token-Stream Intervention Scaffold prior to Tool Execution.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that pre-execution governability is an architectural geometry property fixed at pretraining (`52x` variance across architectures vs. `±0.32x` from LoRA fine-tuning).
Trust_Assumptions: Streaming token interceptor monitors reasoning tokens at 100–200 tokens/s prior to tool-call dispatch.

Study_Title: Kill-Chain Canaries: Stage-Level Tracking of Prompt Injection Across Attack Surfaces and Five Production LLMs
Threat_Attacker_Model: Multi-stage prompt injection propagating across untrusted files/PDFs, agent memory, and inter-agent messages where outcome-only scoring (`0/3` final attack success) masks intermediate kill-chain infection (memory poisoning and sub-agent propagation).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: None (`Kill-Chain Canaries`: stage-level canary tracking across ingestion, memory write, sub-agent relay, and tool execution, plus a 21-feature trajectory classifier audited under leave-one-scenario-out cross-validation).
Enforcement_Point_Location: `Kill-Chain Canary` Stage-Level Instrumentation & Forensic Trajectory Classifier.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Exposes hidden intermediate compromise in multi-agent runs that appear safe under outcome-only grading and proves that trajectory-based drift classifiers fail to generalize across scenarios.
Trust_Assumptions: Canary instrumentation observes intermediate memory writes, inter-agent prompts, and tool arguments.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 5 production LLMs (`GPT-4o-mini`, `GPT-5-mini`, `Claude Haiku 4.5`, `Claude Sonnet 4.5`, `DeepSeek Chat`), stage-level canaries reveal persistent memory and inter-agent infection even when final outcome ASR is `0%` (`0/3` on visible-text PDF for Haiku 4.5; `2/132` on `permission_esc`; `25%` overall ASR on DeepSeek Chat combining `0/24` and `8/8` across channels, pp. 1–5); a 21-feature gradient-boosted trajectory classifier scores `AUC = 0.853` in 5-fold CV (due to model-identity leakage) but collapses to `AUC = 0.39–0.57` (chance level) under strict leave-one-scenario-out evaluation (p. 2, 6).
Exposed_Security_Function: Stage-level kill-chain canary instrumentation across 5 production LLMs and leave-one-scenario-out generalization testing of trajectory classifiers.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Proves a critical negative result: post-hoc trajectory classifiers (`AUC = 0.39–0.57` leave-one-scenario-out) are forensic rather than preventive and cannot generalize to unseen attack scenarios.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 1–4 (pp. 1–2, 5–6): 'A gradient-boosted classifier on 21 trajectory features achieves AUC = 0.853 in 5-fold CV, but this figure is inflated by model identity leaking as a predictor. The stricter evaluation—leave-one-scenario-out—collapses to AUC = 0.39–0.57 (chance level) across all held-out scenarios.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Kill-Chain Canaries track prompt injection stage-by-stage across 5 production LLMs—exposing intermediate memory and sub-agent compromise hidden by 0% outcome-only scores—and prove that trajectory anomaly classifiers collapse from 0.853 AUC (5-fold CV) to 0.39–0.57 AUC (chance level) under leave-one-scenario-out evaluation.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 12-page multi-stage red-teaming and detector generalization study (MIT & UChicago) across 5 production LLMs.
Protected_Object: Untrusted PDF/audio/text inputs, agent memory state, inter-agent messages, and 21 trajectory features.
Composition_Evidence: Tracks attack progression from document ingestion (B1) through memory/inter-agent relay (B2) and tool calls (B3) to forensic auditing (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi teks lengkap PDF (S3-430 / ARXIV-S-0473) terverifikasi SHA-256. Target_Boundary=MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3;B4); Bukti=INFORMAL_ARGUMENT; Maturitas=CONTROLLED_BENCHMARK; PQC=NOT_DISCUSSED; Status=SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE (AD;UG).

Study_Title: Not an A11y: How Android Accessibility Exposes Mobile AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
Threat_Attacker_Model: Indirect prompt injection against mobile AI agents via the Android Accessibility (`A11y`) tree, where malicious developers embed invisible or off-screen `contentDescription` / accessibility metadata (`vectors A1–A3`) that the mobile agent ingests even when invisible on the visual screen.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: None (empirical attack evaluation across Android Accessibility tree vectors `A1–A3`, comparing text-only A11y parsing against multimodal Vision + Reasoning configurations).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Android Accessibility (`A11y`) UI Tree Ingestion & Mobile Agent Action Planner.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates high vulnerability of mobile AI agents to invisible Android Accessibility metadata injection and quantifies the partial mitigation effect of combining Vision with Reasoning.
Trust_Assumptions: Victim mobile agent uses Android Accessibility services to read third-party app UI hierarchies.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across mobile agent configurations (`Gemma4:31B` and `Qwen3.6:35B`, p. 7), Android Accessibility tree injection achieves `0.85–0.90` ASR on `Gemma4:31B` (`FastAgent` without/with Vision) and drops only to `0.62` ASR under `Reasoning with Vision` (from `0.89`); on `Qwen3.6:35B`, `FastAgent with Vision` reduces ASR from `0.55` to `0.43` while `Reasoning with Vision` reduces ASR from `0.58` to `0.51`.
Exposed_Security_Function: Android Accessibility (`A11y`) tree injection across runtime vectors `A1–A3` and multimodal vision/reasoning ablation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Resolved UNMAPPED in DAFTAR_442 to MULTI_BOUNDARY (B1;B2;B3). Even with multimodal Vision + Reasoning enabled, residual ASR remains `0.43–0.62` (43%–62%) because the agent still ingests the poisoned A11y tree alongside the screenshot.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 4–5 (p. 7): 'For Gemma4:31B, adding vision does not reduce ASR in the FastAgent setting: ASR increases slightly from 0.85 to 0.9. In contrast, Reasoning with Vision reduces ASR from 0.89 to 0.62. For Qwen3.6:35B, FastAgent with Vision reduces ASR from 0.55 to 0.43, while Reasoning with Vision reduces ASR only slightly, from 0.58 to 0.51.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Demonstrates that invisible payloads in the Android Accessibility (`A11y`) tree hijack mobile AI agents at 0.55–0.90 ASR across Gemma4:31B and Qwen3.6:35B, and that adding multimodal Vision + Reasoning still leaves a 0.43–0.62 residual ASR.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 12-page mobile agent vulnerability study (Radboud University) evaluating Android Accessibility tree injection vectors across vision and reasoning modes.

Study_Title: ADF-EA: A Unified Execution Assurance System for Agent Device Foundation
Threat_Attacker_Model: Ambiguous physical device execution outcomes, duplicate non-idempotent side effects during crash/retry recovery, false completion claims, and unmet precondition drift in multi-device agent workflows.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Unified Execution Assurance System (`ADF-EA`, Huawei) combining a formal state-transition contract system (`Proposition 1` Ambiguity Impossibility, `Theorem 1` Completion Soundness, `Theorem 2` Recovery Authorization Soundness, pp. 10, 16) with a hash-linked evidence ledger (`Table 1`, p. 4).
Enforcement_Point_Location: `ADF-EA` Transition-System Controller, Post-Condition Observation Verifier, and Hash-Linked Evidence Ledger.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves that duplicate physical effects are prevented under outcome ambiguity (`Proposition 1`), every authorized completion satisfies post-condition contracts (`Theorem 1`), and every recovery re-execution is sound (`Theorem 2`).
Trust_Assumptions: Device observation probes and hash-linked evidence ledger accurately report physical state transitions under assumptions `A1–A5`.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Proves `Proposition 1` and `Theorems 1–2` (pp. 10–16) and evaluates across `17` controlled fault/recovery conditions (`Table 3`, p. 19), native device cases (`Table 4`), skill dispatches (`Table 5`), and multi-branch workflows (`F1–F6`, p. 31), achieving `0` false completions and `0` contract-violating re-executions where baseline agent harnesses commit duplicate or unverified physical effects.
Exposed_Security_Function: Formal execution-assurance transition system (`ADF-EA`) with post-condition observation contracts and hash-linked evidence logging.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Soundness guarantees (`Theorems 1–2`) require explicit per-device observability contracts (`A1–A5`); when physical outcome ambiguity cannot be resolved by sensors (`Proposition 1`), `ADF-EA` safely halts/abstains rather than proceeding autonomously.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 2–4 (pp. 4, 10, 16, 18–23, Proposition 1, Theorems 1–2, Tables 1–6): 'Proposition 1 (ambiguity impossibility)... Theorem 1 (completion soundness). Under A1–A5, every completion authorized by the transition system at time t satisfies... Theorem 2 (recovery authorization soundness). Under A1–A4, every authorized physical reexecution in the represented system is safe...'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Huawei's ADF-EA formalizes device-agent execution assurance with a hash-linked evidence ledger, proving Ambiguity Impossibility (Proposition 1), Completion Soundness (Theorem 1), and Recovery Authorization Soundness (Theorem 2) and eliminating false completions and unsafe retries across 17 fault conditions.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 61-page formal and systems paper (Huawei) proving Proposition 1 and Theorems 1–2 and evaluating ADF-EA across 17 controlled fault/recovery conditions and multi-branch device workflows.
Protected_Object: Heterogeneous device commands, pre/post-condition observation contracts, recovery transitions, and hash-linked evidence ledgers.
Composition_Evidence: Governs skill/command delegation (B2), physical device execution & recovery (B3), and hash-linked evidence ledger auditing (B4).

Study_Title: From Approval to Execution: Reconstruction-Aware Repair Analysis for LLM-Agent Software
Threat_Attacker_Model: Approval-to-execution Time-of-Check-to-Time-of-Use (`TOCTOU`) mutations in LLM-agent frameworks (e.g., Vercel AI SDK, LangGraph, Lobster) where workflow reload, transcript projection, argument rebinding, or durable-state lookup reconstructs and mutates the approved action object before sink execution.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Reconstruction-aware static/symbolic repair soundness analysis (`Pres(h, pi)`) verifying whether an approval handle `h` binds an immutable snapshot or `HMAC`-authenticated payload all the way to the execution sink.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Approval-to-Execution Reconstruction Analyzer & `HMAC`-Bound Snapshot Enforcer.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Decides repair sufficiency (`FS` vs. `FU`) across approval-to-execution reconstruction paths and prevents post-approval argument mutation (`15/15` mutations blocked when `HMAC` secret binding is enforced).
Trust_Assumptions: Framework control/data-flow graph (`CFG`/projection edges) and `HMAC` secret key are intact.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across `28` frozen topology-intervention cases (`Table 1`, p. 11), reconstruction-aware analysis accurately predicts repair sufficiency (`Wilson 95% CI [0.88, 1.00]`, `F1 = 0.974` on `20` cases in `Table 2`, p. 13), and in the live Vercel AI SDK / Octokit evaluation (p. 14), omitting the `HMAC` secret allows `15 / 15` post-approval mutations to reach the execution sink whereas enforcing `HMAC` binding passes `5 / 5` exact executions and blocks `15 / 15` (`100%`) mutations before executor entry.
Exposed_Security_Function: Reconstruction-aware approval-to-execution path analysis (`Pres(h, pi)`) and `HMAC`-authenticated snapshot binding.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Shallow AST graph extractor requires manual/abstention handling on 3 dynamic reflection cases (`Table 2`, p. 13), and uses classical `HMAC` (`STAGE_0_PRE_QUANTUM_ONLY`).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 3–6 (pp. 1, 6, 11–14, Tables 1–2): 'Yet the action shown for approval is often not the object ultimately consumed: workflow reload, transcript projection, argument rebinding, and durable-state lookup may reconstruct it before execution... On the 28 frozen topology–intervention cases... F1 0.974... without its documented secret, 15/15 mutations reach the Octokit recorder; with HMAC, exact execution succeeds in 5/5 and all mutations fail before executor entry.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Formalizes approval-to-execution state reconstruction vulnerabilities across LLM-agent frameworks, achieving 0.974 F1 across 28 repair-sufficiency cases and showing that HMAC-authenticated approval binding blocks 15/15 post-approval argument mutations that otherwise reach the execution sink.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: 18-page program-analysis and runtime-enforcement study evaluating approval-to-execution reconstruction repairs across 28 topology-intervention cases and live SDK sinks.
Protected_Object: Human approval dialogs, durable workflow snapshots, HMAC-bound approval tokens, and tool execution sinks.
Composition_Evidence: Guarantees that the action approved by the user at B1 survives state reconstruction across B2 to match the exact object executed at B3.

Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang independen oleh REVIEWER_1 dan rekonsiliasi adjudikasi lintas-reviewer Stage 3.
